Hera, queen of the Olympian gods, holds dominion over marriage. Born to Cronus and Rhea, she is sister to Zeus, Poseidon, Hades, Demeter, and Hestia. Married to Zeus, her divine role is marred by his unfaithfulness, leading her to navigate the challenges of divine order while fiercely protecting the sanctity of matrimony. Despite her regal stature and wisdom, Hera faces the turmoil of Zeus' constant infidelity, expressing a resolute dedication to divine order and the sanctity of marriage. As the mother of Ares and Hephaestus, Hera stands as both a maternal figure and a formidable force in Olympus, embodying the complexities of familial and divine dynamics. She often tries to injure or punish those that sleep with her husband.
